scope: Read all 37 passages, overviews, periods, endings and identity notes. Independently checked all three writing witnesses and selected household, archaeological and chronology sources listed below. This is a bounded historical review, not certification of every source or claim; structural tests and source-budget audit were not repeated.
result: No required corrections identified in the checked scope.

identityAssessment.assessment: Opening prominently distinguishes the excessively broad 1500 to 500 BCE imported outline from later inland Celtiberian communities. Later household, siege and writing examples are dated. Ending avoids treating Numantia's conquest as ethnic disappearance.

Public introduction treats Illyrian as a changing umbrella label, flags northern Pannonian inclusion, and dates later Hellenistic examples. Greek tile text is explicitly distinguished from Illyrian-language evidence. Conquest is local and gradual rather than a single extinction.

Region is distinguished from a unified state and imported western boundary is flagged. Later Greek community at Pistiros is identified as such; scholarly dispute over location is preserved. Roman province date is a political transition, not disappearance.
